The forecast runs inside the Forge function (1.75.0-1.77.3)
nodes.rationale: Existing Python under Pyodide inside the function: one implementation of every figure, no remote, no egress, Runs on Atlassian badge earned when the remotes block leaves the manifest. Chosen after a throwaway probe showed byte-identical figures on WebAssembly.

nodes.label: Sequencing runs as an async job (1.77.0)
nodes.rationale: Cubic in ask count; twelve asks is three and a half minutes on Forge's CPU so no synchronous resolver answers it. Resolver validates via /v1/sequence-check, pushes to a queue, answers 202; sequence-fn consumer under 900s/1024MB reads retry context first; adapter polls so src/app.js is untouched. Titles never enter the event, only the job row inside the tenant.

nodes.label: The forecast is a job with a chunked payload (1.77.3)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous in-function forecast took 12-15s on the dev board: 906 sparse observations and 31 open items make forecast_completion walk ~280 days per trial, five million draws. ADR 0031's 'facts and forecast stay synchronous' corrected. Payload (a team's whole history) exceeds the 100KB event limit so it travels through app storage in 160KB chunks, capped at 4MB.

nodes.label: WebAssembly parity suite tests/test_wasm.py (1.76.2)
nodes.rationale: Regenerates forge/src/assets.js, answers every service route natively via routes.answer and through forge/src/runtime.js under snapshot and plain loads, and compares strings byte for byte; asserts every .py in agent/tools/ is in the bundle.

nodes.label: Python runtime packed into forge/src/assets.js (1.76.1)
nodes.rationale: build-assets.mjs gzips the pinned pyodide 314.0.6 package, agent/tools/ and routes.py into a git-ignored module with a memory snapshot; git-ignored because a second copy of the Python drifts. Boot sequence is one string shared by loader and generator.

nodes.label: service/routes.py split from app.py (1.76.0)
nodes.rationale: Routes, caps and refusals ending in answer(path, body) are what a Forge function runs under WebAssembly; HTTP, auth verifiers and body limit stay in app.py which adds nothing to any envelope. Test holds handle() and answer() byte-identical.

nodes.label: Sequencing capped at twelve asks, in the tool (1.75.1/1.76.0)
nodes.rationale: Second probe measured 1.1/7/21/48s natively for 4/8/12/16 asks and ten times that on Forge; the fifty the service allowed was 25 minutes nobody had run. intake.MAX_ASKS and too_many_asks() so every transport refuses at the same number in the same words.

nodes.label: GB realm declared with its own London service (1.73.0-1.74.1)
nodes.rationale: Atlassian's EU realm is Frankfurt and Dublin; the UK is a separate realm and the September trial is a UK company. Pointing GB at Frankfurt was rejected as a quiet lie against the strongest security-review sentence: Forge picks the region at install and the app never gets it wrong. Major version, free while the only install is development.

nodes.label: Calculator keeps its *.run.app hostnames (1.73.0)
nodes.rationale: A custom domain would be the only indirection between manifest and infrastructure, but a project migrated into a Google organisation keeps its id and resource URLs, so only recreating the project moves them; declined in writing rather than insured at £30-40 a month.

nodes.label: forge/manifest.yml triggers the deploy for the guard (1.74.2)
nodes.rationale: The realm guard lives in deploy.yml which did not trigger on manifest changes, so the one commit that declared GB was the one it sat out; a typo would have routed a UK tenant at an unverified hostname for up to a week.

nodes.label: Burndown moved into metrics.burndown and served by /v1/burndown (1.72.0)
nodes.rationale: The tile had been blank on every Forge install with a sentence blaming the tenant's data. The algorithm existed three times already; a resolver copy would be a fourth in a fourth language. A period with no clock is refused, never answered with an empty series. burndownNote always travels, null when nothing to explain.

nodes.label: metrics.burndown threw on Forge for want of a fixture (1.72.1)
nodes.rationale: orgconfig.working_days returns dates, the helper it replaced returned ISO strings; every dataset in the repo carries meta.workingDays so the deriving branch had no fixture and the parity test exercised the other one. Test now runs both branches and asserts identical rows.

nodes.label: creditableEpics reports what it excluded via valueWindow (1.71.0)
nodes.rationale: MOBL Sprint 4 closed before its planned start, so three finished epics worth $245k fell outside a date window that could not contain them and were dropped by a bare continue; the tile blamed the only priced thing in view. The exclusion is now returned and named; valueWindow is Forge-only in the parity check.

nodes.label: Refusal carries the unit it counted in (1.71.0)
nodes.rationale: '11 observations, 10 needed' disproved itself: an `or` reported the item pair whichever of two thresholds (8 working days, 10 items) failed. Each is now two conditions with two sentences; the invariant asserted is have < need.

nodes.label: A key a producer emits and no consumer takes fails a test (1.70.0)
nodes.rationale: Three silent drops in one session: orgConfigOf whitelist, missing asks_considered, setup never assigned. Every top-level key a resolver body carries must be taken off the response by its consumer, and every key the sequencing tile reads must be added by both transports or named one-sided.

nodes.label: Value tile diagnoses three states via editmeta (1.69.1)
nodes.rationale: Field on no screen (admin adds it), field not on the site (app not installed or orgConfig name wrong), or answerable and unanswered; asked only when it would change what a reader is told.

nodes.label: A t-shirt band declares candidacy (1.69.0)
nodes.rationale: Choosing a size is already a statement about work being weighed, so charging a second field buys nothing; reverses ADR 0028's refusal to infer, recorded as an amendment. No/N/False added so it is reversible out loud; candidate_answer returns None for silence, not False.

nodes.label: T-shirt band selects a quartile of completed epics (1.68.0)
nodes.rationale: Reference-class sizing gave every Jira ask the same distribution so orderings differed only by queue and dates. A band picks which quartile of the board's own completed epics, asserting no number; costs eight completed epics; unreadable bands fall back to the whole class and are named.

nodes.label: Value and basis rendered on the sequencing tile (1.67.0)
nodes.rationale: sequence had carried value and valueBasis since it was written and nothing read them. Two shape bugs found by rendering: loopback added asks_considered/board/boardName and Forge did not; the page carried a transport-specific sentence naming data/asks/.

nodes.label: Candidates were filtered out by the resolution-date window (1.66.1)
nodes.rationale: Epics are fetched separately and kept when finished inside the period, the right rule for value; a candidate has no resolution date so the filter excluded every one, always. Kept now when finished in window or reached for.

nodes.label: Forge sequencing delegates to /v1/sequence (1.66.0)
nodes.rationale: Candidacy decided inside the tenant costs a JS mirror of candidateAnswer/candidateIssues/asksFromIssues. Asks are built rather than projected so assertNoFreeText never saw them; assertAsksCarryNoText and _refuse_ask_text close that door. Two refusals: nothing marked, one marked.

nodes.label: A declared candidate becomes an ask (1.65.0)
nodes.rationale: Every required field comes off the board: summary, board, reference-class sizing, the two declared value fields, dueDate. valueEstimate is present or absent, never half; a delivered candidate is still a candidate.

nodes.label: Inline style attributes discarded under Forge CSP (1.64.0)
nodes.rationale: A Custom UI iframe's style-src has no unsafe-inline, so 155 style attributes were silently dropped: bars lost fills, severity discs lost colour. Fixed by wrapping the innerHTML setter once to re-apply via el.style.cssText, only where detection shows the attribute did not survive; relaxing the policy was rejected.

nodes.label: The app declares a Candidate field (1.63.0)
nodes.rationale: Candidacy is a state not a type: sequencing on issue type would order decisions already taken. orgConfig.askField defaults to the app's text field or names a site's own checkbox; Yes/Y/True, empty is not a candidate, anything else is neither and is named.

nodes.label: The fetcher reads the two declared fields and fetches epics (1.62.0)
nodes.rationale: It wrote businessValue: 0 on every issue, and metrics decides measured-from-unmeasured on key presence, so every file claimed the sprint delivered nothing worth anything. Key omitted when no field, null when unfilled; matched on field key never display name; epics fetched separately on both pull paths.

nodes.label: Reader can restate what each status means (1.60.0/1.61.0)
nodes.rationale: Inferred statuses are disclosed in a Workflow chip and the footer (the chip does not print); the mapping edits the dataset's own orgConfig.statuses and re-derives from the data as it arrived, not the view, because a view-level toggle gives two readers different completion figures and the file may use no browser storage.

nodes.label: orgConfigOf dropped four organisation keys (1.59.0)
nodes.rationale: It named four keys and built a fresh object; countSubtasks, countedTypes, valueFromHierarchy and trendSprints were discarded, so a site counted subtasks in the facts pack and not on the page. e2e now moves all four and compares the whole merged config to orgconfig.merge.

nodes.label: Jira's field list answers 200 anonymously (1.58.0)
nodes.rationale: A bad credential did not fail; it flattened the burndown, because /rest/api/3/field answers anonymously with no custom fields and find_fields printed one warning. whoami() proves the connection is somebody before any data call. Also: the secret scan now asks git rather than walking the tree, so a configured .env does not fail make test.

nodes.label: Migration to /rest/api/3/search/jql pages by token (1.56.0)
nodes.rationale: The old endpoint paged by index with a total; the new one has no total so body.get('total',0) would stop after one page, reporting 100 issues as the whole board. The walk ends on the absence of a token and a page cap raises rather than returning a partial board.

nodes.label: The app declares a Value Basis field, free text (1.57.0)
nodes.rationale: Not read from the issue description because that would make 'no basis recorded' unsayable. Two field ids travel as one named pair; cost was stated as major and corrected in 1.57.1: a second entry under a declared module block is minor.

nodes.label: Epics are not on a scrum board so they are fetched separately (1.55.0)
nodes.rationale: Declaring the value field was necessary and not sufficient: the sprint issue endpoint never returns an epic. Items and value are two pools; history_row was counting an epic as an item. read:epic:jira-software added to the allow-list.

nodes.label: Value tile printed '-1 of the 0 completed items' (1.55.1)
nodes.rationale: Subtracted the value pool from the item pool after ADR 0026 split them; both sides come from the value pool now and the tile says where value is recorded.

nodes.label: The app declares a Business Value field (1.54.0)
nodes.rationale: Declared via jira:customField rather than created via REST, which would need Administer Jira; found by module key never by display name; unset is null not 0; counted at hierarchy level 1 and above.

nodes.label: Business Value was declared, read, and never requested (1.54.1)
nodes.rationale: A field in the projection that nothing asks Jira for is invisible permanently and silently; test_service holds projection and request together.

nodes.label: Issue-type filter that changes what is counted (1.53.0)
nodes.rationale: Types read off the loaded issues; selection travels with the forecast and is in both cache keys; a reader narrows the organisation's rule and never widens it; selecting nothing is a refusal. Exposed that filter dropdowns were built once and never rebuilt across boards.

nodes.label: Subtasks were counted as items everywhere (1.52.0)
nodes.rationale: Item counting could be inflated by decomposing generously, and whether subtasks even arrive depends on board type and route, so two customers got two definitions of throughput. countSubtasks defaults false, countedTypes empty allow-list, Jira's own flag not the name, counting disclosure printed always.

nodes.label: Cross-team roll-up names its boards and refuses to forecast (1.50.0/1.51.0)
nodes.rationale: The app cannot know which boards it is not seeing, so names make omission unnecessary to detect. Carries no team label so team_slice cannot narrow silently, and pooling teams' throughput is not a valid sample anyway. Windows excluded because three overlapping windows triple a board.

nodes.label: SSO needs nothing built (1.49.0)
nodes.rationale: The app owns no identity: the panel is opened by someone Atlassian authenticated, the calculator authenticates callers not people. Suite asserts no password, token, cookie, session or environment credential in forge/; the token path exists only in scripts/.

nodes.label: Activity log, deliberately not called an audit log (1.48.0)
nodes.rationale: Jira's audit API is read-only and reading it needs Administer Jira, so an app-written best-effort log it can also rewrite is not tamper-evident; the tile says so. Bounded at 1000 with a cumulative droppedTotal in the store.

nodes.label: The anchor issue is the brief's access control (1.47.0)
nodes.rationale: Jira enforces browse on the anchor at send time. Per-recipient composition via asUser(accountId) impersonation exists and is deferred, not rejected; checking recipients' permissions needs Administer Jira and still would not answer the question. Test fails if allowImpersonation appears.

nodes.label: Forecast log claims carry view width (1.46.0)
nodes.rationale: A claim is made once and resolved once, never rescored, so the irreversible hazard is resolving a good claim from a narrow view. Narrower claims are not published; narrower resolutions are left pending.

nodes.label: A recorded row records how wide the view was (1.45.0)
nodes.rationale: A row written by a narrow reader is wrong, not merely leaky, and smaller in the same direction as bad delivery. issuesSeen: a narrower view never replaces a row, a wider view corrects one (the one exception to never rewriting), a reader who sees less is told so.

nodes.label: Permission mirroring holds by accident where nothing is kept (1.44.0)
nodes.rationale: Every panel read is asUser so Jira decides; the durable series and forecast log broke that by storing one viewer's aggregate for everyone. Every app-level store is declared with what it exposes, including orgConfig which is a Jira property.

nodes.label: trendSprints replaces three silent six-sprint caps (1.43.0)
nodes.rationale: Default six, bounded two to forty; a sprint outside the window and one missing from inside it get different sentences; a board with more sprints than the window says so.

nodes.label: The forecast log is written and scored (1.41.0/1.42.0)
nodes.rationale: Logged as capacity claims (p% of at least N items by D) holding no issue identity so item 4 stays off item 5's path; claim id deterministic on context, day and percentile; a what-if writes nothing; refusals are not logged; resolution runs against the latest date each transport's data can speak to; bounded at 400 and says what it dropped.

nodes.label: history_row moved into agent/tools/metrics.py (1.37.0)
nodes.rationale: A Forge tenant has no Python so rows come from the calculator, which ships agent/tools/ only. series.js stays pure storage policy; seriesNote counting rows into a sentence was a figure between a tool and a reader and moved to merge_series/series_note in Python.

nodes.label: A Forge tenant has a trend (1.38.0-1.39.2)
nodes.rationale: history is a route of its own, not a field on the context body. series_upto slices per selected context after a served board-wide series compared a June sprint against September; history_series sorts by start date because the two callers disagreed about order; every context that produces no row is named with its reason.

nodes.label: The image takes Debian's security updates at build time (1.39.0)
nodes.rationale: Every push failed the scan on a fixable OpenSSL CVE no base image had rebuilt for; alpine failed the same gate and distroless scanned worse. apt upgrade in the build, never dist-upgrade; suppressing the finding refused because the first waved-through CVE makes the gate advisory.

nodes.label: History rows derived from dates keyed to a moment (1.36.0)
nodes.rationale: Rows derived from current status made a closed sprint look better the longer ago it was. Four implementations collapsed into history_row(); both fixture generators wrote issues done tomorrow. ADR 0015 rewritten around the four things that genuinely do not survive re-derivation.

nodes.label: Recipient picker takes a name and shows who ids are (1.31.0-1.35.0)
nodes.rationale: Searching as the reader so Jira's Browse users permission decides; matches projected through a two-field allow-list; deactivated accounts shown in the config list but filtered from search; every id gets a row because user/bulk omits unmatched ids; nothing calls render() because the tile is a form in progress.

nodes.label: A brief was delivered through Jira (1.30.0-1.32.0)
nodes.rationale: Six failures none the obvious thing: reasons reached nobody three times, 'stop' is OpenAI's word not end_turn, refusal is its own category, a slot named p85 made the model write 85, forecast-context nests under sprint_completion, mutation testing measured by grep not exit status. The site's outgoing mail was the last blocker.

nodes.label: A negative result from synthetic input against an embedded frame is not evidence (1.29.1-1.29.5)
nodes.rationale: Four diagnoses across four entries, three wrong, chasing a scrolling bug that did not exist: wheel and key events never reached the cross-origin iframe and the screenshot coordinate space shifted. Settled by a person with a mouse.

nodes.label: The scheduled brief reads the board as the app (1.29.0)
nodes.rationale: Reverses ADR 0013's addendum because restrict {BROWSE} on every notification makes who receives a brief Jira's decision. jira(as) replaces nine asUser sites, defaulted to user; a structural test walks every call to an enclosing function declaring as.

nodes.label: Each board has its own recipients set by a project administrator (1.28.0)
nodes.rationale: Gate is Jira's mypermissions answer, havePermission === true exactly, asked again on write; viewers see the config read-only; the tile validates nothing; loopback saves over POST while the bridge invoke() has no verb.

nodes.label: Jira sends the brief through /notify (1.26.0)
nodes.rationale: No SMTP needed and the brief never leaves Atlassian; recipients are Jira identities so the config holds no contact details; restrict is constant and partial; the cost is attachments so the view ships as static HTML. Read-only scope rule became a justified allow-list.

nodes.label: Mail subject flattened against header injection (1.27.0)
nodes.rationale: A board name with CRLF would close the Subject header; escaping does nothing for a header. Found by writing the test; mutation testing showed the body escape was unexercised by a fixture with hostile text only in the board name.

nodes.label: The model never writes a number (1.24.0)
nodes.rationale: A brief is a template with named slots filled by substitution in code; the model writes only the sentences between. Checking numerals afterwards was rejected because passing a wrong number in the permissive direction is the worst failure class. Refused sections never reach the model's output path; the number-word list is whole-word and names what it cannot catch.

nodes.label: Forge LLMs write the brief inside the tenant (1.24.0)
nodes.rationale: The obvious implementation was an API key and third-party egress of every issue title weekly; @forge/llm runs Atlassian-hosted Claude with no egress, so the crossing does not happen. Adding the llm module is a major version.

nodes.label: A scheduled trigger needs its own function (1.25.0-1.25.2)
nodes.rationale: weekly-brief pointed at the resolver whose dispatcher expects {call:{functionKey}} and threw on every fire; proved by shortening the interval to fiveMinute because absent logs cannot distinguish broken from idle. 1.25.1's diagnosis from silence was a plausible story fitted to missing data.

nodes.label: /v1/slice lets the calculator choose the team slice (1.23.0)
nodes.rationale: The resolver must fetch issues before asking for a forecast but the slice is the calculator's decision; the route takes contexts and an id, no issues, and returns ids to fetch, so there is no second copy of team_slice which had been wrong twice.

nodes.label: team_slice and forecast_for moved to agent/tools/selection.py (1.22.0)
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile copies agent/tools/ only, so the slice had to live there or be written a second time in JavaScript; the first tool module that is not a calculation. /v1/forecast-context refuses rather than guessing in the three places guessing would produce a number.

nodes.label: The calculator is reached by invokeRemote (1.19.0)
nodes.rationale: callCalculator used plain fetch against process.env.CALCULATOR_URL which sends no Authorization header, so a real baseUrl would 401 in every mode. invokeRemote with operations: [compute] attaches the token, and a manifest baseUrl is chosen per install from the customer's residency.

nodes.label: The calculator verifies Forge invocation tokens (1.18.0-1.21.0)
nodes.rationale: Returns who the caller is, not a boolean. Twelve forgery cases against a signer the suite controls; the tenant claim is nested app.installationId and the flat lookup passed every test while unable to read a real token. Eight hand-made tokens refused live, six in 0ms because the algorithm is pinned before a key lookup.

nodes.label: The calculator is hosted on Cloud Run (1.20.0-1.20.3)
nodes.rationale: Two regions, scale to zero; forecast byte-identical across three machines and two continents. Cold start measured at 1.15s and 0.39s against a 25s token budget, the argument for min-instances=0.

nodes.label: The service refused the correct credential over a trailing newline (1.20.2)
nodes.rationale: _verify_shared_secret stripped the presented token and not the configured one; provision-gcp.sh piped openssl rand with its newline into Secret Manager. Both sides fixed; a whitespace-only secret is still no secret.

nodes.label: Sizing groups epics by epicKey when names are stripped (1.17.1)
nodes.rationale: intake grouped by the epic summary, which clean_dataset strips, so over the Forge route every t-shirt scale and reference class refused. The field is chosen once for the whole issue set because a per-issue fallback would split one epic in two and shrink every band.

nodes.label: Four flow tiles that need no sprint (1.17.0)
nodes.rationale: Cycle time scatter ranked above cumulative flow because it yields a sentence a team can take outward; CFD has three bands and says so; Little's Law reconciled with no verdict drawn. Blocked time, flow distribution by type, WIP limits and a per-person cut deliberately left out.

nodes.label: A board with no sprints gets 14/30/90-day windows (1.16.4-1.16.11)
nodes.rationale: A window bounds the selection, round-trips through an id like SFT/2/win:30d, and carries no working-day list, because giving it one printed Pace vs clock -45pp for a team that committed to nothing. Delivered % refuses because a window's membership is partly defined by being done. Three overlapping windows must never be rolled up. Tiles that can never measure a flow board are hidden and named, not refused in place.

nodes.label: Flow-board forecast counted every issue three times (1.16.13)
nodes.rationale: A flow board's three windows hold the same issues so the slice tripled throughput and forecast a p85 of four days against a true ten; issues are de-duplicated by key. A window supplies no default target date, which had answered 0% against a deadline nobody set.

nodes.label: The `or 10` sprint-length fallback removed (1.16.4)
nodes.rationale: A dateless dataset was told to commit to 9 items over '20,000 simulated sprints of 10 working days'; ten is the default fortnight so nobody queried it. Falling back to orgConfig.sprintLengthDays would be the same bug in the config's clothes.

nodes.label: Flow health score for flow boards (1.16.12)
nodes.rationale: Flow efficiency 40%, blockers and ageing 30% each; three components not four dressed as four; flow efficiency is load-bearing so its absence refuses whole rather than passing the half-weight floor. One 40% threshold replaced two (40 and 45).

nodes.label: The dashboard scored an empty sprint 66/100 (1.16.1)
nodes.rationale: Every divide-by-zero guard resolved to good news; 66 looks computed. It is the state the Forge build opens in. Six elements now refuse; e2e sweeps them for digits rather than wording; the faded grid was removed because it put the only text below AA contrast.

nodes.label: A missing calendar was scored as bad delivery (1.16.2)
nodes.rationale: Delivery pace at 34% weight scored 0/100 without dates, turning Amber to Red; an unmeasured component now leaves the composition and is named, survivors re-weighted, below half the weight the score refuses. 'No sprint calendar' was printed for three different causes.

nodes.label: The dashboard inside Forge shows the customer's own Jira (1.16.0)
nodes.rationale: The bridge adapter is a classic CommonJS script required in a try because @forge/bridge throws outside a frame and an ES import aborted the file. sprintsFor distinguished a 400 (kanban) from a 403; board ids built from two endpoints that disagreed about location; the resolver computes only addedMidSprint; story points discovered by name; orgConfig resolved from Jira status categories plus a project property with a second validator held equal to the Python.

nodes.label: The hosted calculator takes a projection and refuses free text (1.15.0)
nodes.rationale: forecast.build over a dataset stripped to ten fields is byte-identical, so no issue title leaves Atlassian; the resolver re-attaches summary and assignee by key. Free text is refused with 400, not dropped, and the two field lists are compared across languages.

nodes.label: Jira connects over OAuth 2.0 3LO (1.14.0)
nodes.rationale: A grant a customer consents to, scoped read-only and revocable; the token path stays supported for one's own board and the fetcher prints which it used. A grant covering two sites is refused rather than resolved.

nodes.label: Organisation config replaces hard-coded assumptions (1.14.0)
nodes.rationale: Adopting it changes no number; a bad config stops the run; holidays shorten working time only; a status the config never saw is named at the end of every fetch. Found forecast.py honouring meta.workingDays in one place and rebuilding Mon-Fri in five others.

nodes.label: Tiles can be put in your own order (1.13.0)
nodes.rationale: Arrows rather than drag and drop for keyboard operability; the nodes move rather than a CSS order so reading order follows the picture; focus survives the move and a live region announces it; ?order= separate from ?tiles=.

nodes.label: The simulation horizon is named when trials abandon (1.11.0)
nodes.rationale: Each trial stops at 400 working days and a request beyond the team's pace returned every percentile at exactly 400; unfinished_fraction is returned and the tile prints 'these dates are a floor'. No-silent-caps applied to the forecaster itself.

nodes.label: The Monte Carlo tile is served, not reimplemented (1.10.0)
nodes.rationale: A second Monte Carlo in JavaScript would be a second set of numbers; the tile does not work in an emailed file and says so. It samples the team's whole history and takes only the outstanding count from the selected sprint, pinned by a test after the 1.8.0 slice bug.

nodes.label: Live server dropped the connection on any 404 (1.9.1)
nodes.rationale: log_message tested substring membership on an HTTPStatus and raised after the 404 was decided; three traversal checks were passing because a dropped connection has no body.

nodes.label: Tiles can be turned off with Executive and Team presets (1.9.0)
nodes.rationale: Presets are the agent's two reports; visibility changes what is shown and nothing counted; a saved view carries the loaded data not the shipped seed; hidden tiles are named.

nodes.label: The Pages workflow is workflow_dispatch only (1.8.1)
nodes.rationale: It copies all of data/ into a public site and a fresh repo only failed because Pages was not enabled; enabling Pages later would have published real issue titles on the next commit.

nodes.label: Product intake forecasts an ask before tickets exist (1.8.0)
nodes.rationale: Sizing ladder with the rung declared (t-shirt, reference class, explicit); two scenarios always; uncertainty attributed by three simulations; readiness gate first; sequencing returns consequences not a score. The intake bundle is separate from the demo bundle so demo forecast figures do not move.

nodes.label: Three intake scope bugs returned plausible wrong numbers (1.8.0)
nodes.rationale: board_issues returned the first context so a 16-item ask forecast at 77 days instead of 19; the interruption rate came from whichever context was last in the file; queue_ahead ignored as_of. Pinned by an intake scope section in test_agent.

nodes.label: Overtime removed, Team load card built from status (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Deleting only the overtime line would have left output-per-person with no counterweight, the individual framing the dashboard refuses; both series went. overtimeHrs and teamPutsSP removed from every schema and document.

nodes.label: Security suite found a real stored XSS (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Risk register and executive bullets interpolated keys and summaries unescaped; fixed with a single escape point at output plus safeUrl() for javascript: schemes.

nodes.label: Accessibility suite found 67 low-contrast nodes (1.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Fixed with separate UI colour tokens so the validated chart palette stayed untouched; severity glyph colour chosen per severity; drill-down close returns focus.
